title: Corsano CardioWatch 287–2 algorithm recognizes a real-life ventricular-fibrillation arrest and collapse in post-processing; the patient's ICD, not the wristband, ended it
summary: Radboudumc DETECT-3 case: a 64-year-old's VF arrest while cycling was ended by his ICD; the CardioWatch PPG algorithm later detected pulselessness at 09:50:17 and the fall; no live alert was sent.
account: Edgar, Jansen, Pol, Pisters, van Royen and Bonnes of Radboud University Medical Center (with Rijnstate Hospital) reported in Resuscitation Plus on 29 January 2026 (the publication date is used; the paper gives no calendar date for the event) the first real-life cardiac arrest captured by a wristband with cardiac-arrest detection. A 64-year-old man with heart failure, permanent atrial fibrillation and a secondary-prevention Biotronik ICD was wearing the CE-certified CardioWatch 287–2 (Corsano Health, The Hague) in the DETECT-3 study. After three weeks, while cycling alone, he developed monomorphic ventricular tachycardia that accelerated to ventricular fibrillation after an antitachycardia pacing burst; the ICD delivered a 40 J shock, he regained consciousness, cycled home, and was admitted for rhythm observation with a good recovery. The wristband's 32 Hz photoplethysmography and accelerometry data were exported afterwards and run, by a Corsano Health data scientist blinded to the event, through the DETECT photoplethysmography algorithm, which detected cardiac arrest at 09:50:17 after loss of pulse and ended the alert at 09:50:57 when pulsations returned; the group's fall-detection algorithm flagged the fall about 8–10 seconds after pulselessness. The authors state the detection was retrospective and that the study collects data to measure false-positive rates for a future live system. Companion papers from the same program report 98% sensitivity in induced circulatory arrests (DETECT-1a), external validation in 50 patients with induced VT/VF (DETECT-1b, April 2026) and 100% sensitivity (23 of 23) with one false positive in true non-shockable arrests after withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment (Lancet Regional Health Europe, July 2026), where the algorithm is described as rule-based. The patient's survival is attributable to the ICD; the wristband changed nothing for him.
purpose: Built to detect out-of-hospital cardiac arrest from wrist photoplethysmography and accelerometry and, in future, alert emergency services; the retrospective detection demonstrates the first half of that purpose.
system: Corsano CardioWatch 287-2 with the DETECT photoplethysmography cardiac-arrest detection and accelerometry fall-detection algorithms
model_version: CardioWatch 287-2 (CE-certified); DETECT algorithm as developed in DETECT-1a
developer: DETECT program, Radboud University Medical Center, with Corsano Health, The Hague (device and algorithm processing)
location: Netherlands (DETECT-3 study, Nijmegen; the cycling incident's location is not named)
segment: Research wristband for automated cardiac-arrest detection
taxonomy_note: A post-hoc detection on one case is read as task performance; nothing changed for the patient.

ratings.reason: The patient was saved by his ICD; the wristband's detection was retrospective and produced no alert or treatment.
The authors argue a live system could act as a first witness for unwitnessed arrests, but no deployment outcome exists yet.

ai_role.statement: The algorithm, run afterwards on exported data by a blinded Corsano data scientist, correctly flagged the loss of pulse and the fall; it was not running live and sent no alert, and the ICD shock is what restored circulation. The developers' own papers are the only full sources, and they describe a rule-based detector of absent pulsations by signal amplitude and waveform morphology rather than a machine-learning model.

produced_by: Continuous wristband wear with 32 Hz photoplethysmography and accelerometry uploaded to a study cloud
A shockable arrest with clear loss of pulsations during cycling, in a patient whose ICD provided the reference and the rescue
Blinded post-hoc processing by the developers' data scientist
must_hold: Adequate photoplethysmography quality during motion (the authors note it is typically disturbed by motion)
A live implementation with acceptable false-positive rates, which DETECT-3 is still measuring
An alerting chain to emergency services, which does not yet exist for this device

headline: Corsano CardioWatch recognizes a VF arrest in post-processing
metric: detected cardiac arrest at 09:50:17 after loss of pulse

comparator.against: the ICD's electrograms and the confirmed time of collapse (velocity 0 km/h), reviewed in post-processing
comparator.after: Cardiac arrest was detected at 09:50:17, after a loss of pulse in the photoplethysmography signal.
comparator.quote: Cardiac arrest was detected at 09:50:17, after a loss of pulse in the photoplethysmography signal. The alert was terminated at 09:50:57, when the return of several normal photoplethysmography peaks was detected. Moreover, the fall with a period of no movement afterwards was detected by our previously developed fall detection algorithm.

later.note: The same group's later prospective validation in ICU patients with non-shockable arrest after withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment reported 100% sensitivity in the 23-patient test set with one false positive, and DETECT-1b (April 2026) externally validated the algorithm in 50 induced shockable arrests; no live alerting has been reported.
later.quote: In the test set, sensitivity was 100% (23/23; 95% CI 82–100%), with one false positive alert.
